_comment: Mutation testing config for the web client. Enforcement lives in the nightly mutation workflow's score-regression gate, so there is no local break threshold. Every carve-out in `mutate` carries a justification in `_mutate_justifications`, keyed by the pattern it explains — the same per-entry discipline agent/.cargo/mutants.toml follows.

_mutate_justifications.!src/**/*.test.ts, !src/**/*.test.tsx, !: Test code. Mutating an assertion measures nothing — the tests are the oracle, not the subject.
_mutate_justifications.!src/types/api.d.ts, !src/types/**/*.d.t: Generated from api/openapi.yaml (npm run generate:api) and type-only: erased at build time, so there is no runtime behavior to mutate. Drift is caught by the OpenAPI regeneration check, not by tests.
_mutate_justifications.!src/main.tsx: Application entry point: createRoot + render wiring with no branching logic. Exercised end to end by the Playwright suite, which every mutant would fail identically.
_mutate_justifications.!src/router.tsx: Route table declaration. Its mutants are route-path string swaps that the Playwright navigation specs already fail on, and no unit test can meaningfully assert a router config in isolation.
_mutate_justifications.!src/components/icons.tsx: SVG path data. Mutants alter `d` attributes and viewBox numbers — visually verified by the Playwright screenshot suite, not assertable in a unit test.
_mutate_justifications.!src/features/terminal/use-terminal.ts: xterm.js binding: constructs a Terminal, attaches a FitAddon, and wires DOM resize observers. The behavior lives in xterm's own canvas/DOM rendering, which jsdom does not implement, so there is no in-tree harness that could kill a mutant. Covered end to end by the terminal Playwright spec.
_mutate_justifications.!src/features/remote-desktop/use-remote-: Canvas wiring: the effect bails out at canvas.getContext('2d'), which jsdom returns null for, so no mutant downstream of that line can ever execute in a unit test. Every part with testable logic is factored out and mutated on its own — desktop-worker.ts for the paint path and input-handler.ts for the event capture — and the wiring itself is covered by the remote-desktop Playwright spec.
